modern

memory, recollection
to be, to exist
town, neighborhood

October 10, 1964, was the day the opening ceremony of the Tokyo Olympics was held.
Expresses that it would be better not to do something: 'it was better not to (rain)'
Indicates an objective reason or cause: 'because... so...'
Embeds a question into the main sentence: 'to see what month and day...'
Because it was better for it not to rain on this day, the person in charge looked into which dates were usually sunny.
Deciding on a specific option or time: 'to decide on...'
And then, they decided on October 10th.
Expresses a tendency or characteristic: 'easy to...', 'likely to...'
Conveys hearsay or reported information: 'I heard that...'
October 10th also tends to be sunny, but reportedly October 15th is even more likely to be sunny.
prone to being sunny, likely to be clear
To become, to be decided as
Why was October 10th chosen, I wonder?
do not know, do not understand
Expresses an objective cause or reason: 'because...', 'since...'
Potential pattern expressing ability or possibility: 'can do...', 'to be able to do...'
Since it is a day off, many people can watch the Olympics on TV.
can do, to be able to
When..., at the time of... (indicates a point in time in the past)
To join, to enter somewhere (takes the particle に)
When I was in high school, I joined a very strict volleyball club.
To tell/instruct someone to do something (here conjugated in the passive 言われる: to be told to do something)
Even without doing..., even if not... (expresses concession, negative form of 〜ても)
To go somewhere to do something (here connecting clauses using the て-form: 行って)
In my first year, even without being told by our teacher to practice, I went to school early every morning to practice.
even without being told, even if not told
Placed at the end of a sentence to explain a reason or cause: 'Because...', 'It is because...'
That was because everyone was short.
was short, was low (past tense of い-adjective: 低い)
Concessive pattern meaning 'even if / even though...'. Here it is conjugated into the negative potential form 勝てなくても (even if [one] cannot win).
Nominalizes a verb phrase: 'the act of having done...', used as the subject of the sentence.
Emphatic listing structure: 'both... and...', here used as 朝も夜も (both morning and night).
However, even if we couldn't win any matches, practicing together with everyone morning and night is my fondest memory of high school.
even if (one) cannot win, even without winning
high school days, high school years
To become (for な-adjectives, replace な with に + なる)
Wanted to do something (past tense of the desiderative form V-たい)
I wanted to quickly become good like my seniors.
Only, just (specifically referring only to the first-year group)
Can do, to be able to do (potential form of the verb する)
Moreover, the time when just us first-year students could enjoy practicing together was special.
can practice, to be able to practice
For, in order to (indicates a purpose or intended reason)
Nominalizes a verb (waking up: 起きるの)
Even if..., even though... (expresses concession with na-adjectives: 大変でも)
For the sake of this special time, even though getting up early was tough, I went every morning.
to wake up, to get up
Before... (indicates a point in time or an event that occurs prior)
Indicates doing an action together (together with everyone: みんなで)
And then, before class, everyone ate their breakfast bento together.
Indicates cause or reason (tired from practice)
After doing... (directly modifies the following noun)
The bento we had after getting tired from practice was delicious.
After... (indicates a point in time following an event or period)
Also, too (emphasizes that there was practice after class in addition to the morning)
There was also practice after class.
Together with someone (indicates a partner in an action)
We practiced together with our seniors.
Even though..., despite... (expresses regret or an outcome contrary to expectations/efforts)
Cannot become (negative potential form of になる)
Non-exhaustive listing of nouns (such as... and...)
Even though we practiced and played many practice matches, we couldn't become a strong team.
Pattern expressing the existence of a person or animal at a location ('there is / are... in/at...').
In Japan, there are mascots in various towns.
Used to name or identify something: 'called...', 'named...'.
Modifier describing shape or appearance: 'in the shape of...', 'shaped like...'.
For example, in Imabari City, Ehime Prefecture, there is a bird-shaped mascot called "Bary-san".
Pattern expressing purpose: 'in order to...', 'for the purpose of...'.
Passive voice: expresses an action being "created / made" (つくられました).
Bary-san was created to promote the good points of Imabari City.
Follows a number/counter to indicate "from that amount and up / over...".
Hearsay reporting pattern: "I heard that... / it is said that...".
Such mascots are called "Yuru-chara," and it is said that there are over 1,000 of them.
this kind of, such, like this
to exist, to have, there is
Pattern used to express thoughts or impressions: "to think that... / to feel that...".
Conjunction indicating cause or reason: "because... / since...".
Passive voice: indicates the state of being loved by others (みんなに愛されている).
Because Yuru-chara have faces and shapes that almost everyone finds cute, they are loved by all.
Particle indicating role or capacity: "as... / in the role of..." (おみやげで: as a souvenir).
Passive voice: indicates items "being sold / displayed for sale".
When traveling, lots of Yuru-chara snacks and keychains are sold as souvenirs.
Indirect question embedded in a sentence: "whether... / which / how...".
In addition, there are also events where Yuru-chara from various towns gather to compete for which mascot is the most popular.
to exist, to have, to be
Pattern for listing representative actions or states: "doing things like... and...".
Expresses conjecture or possibility: "might, may, perhaps...".
If that town's mascot becomes famous, souvenirs might sell well, or many people might come to visit the mascot.
Money will likely flow into the town.
Pattern for giving a typical example or comparison: "such as... / like...".
Expresses a change of state: "to become..." (必要になる: to become necessary).
Expresses an ongoing state or developing trend: "is becoming... / is currently...".
Mascots like "yuru-chara" are becoming essential for Japanese towns.
Conditional/hypothetical pattern; in this sentence, expresses discovering something unexpected (mother being in the room) after carrying out an action (returning home).
Last Friday, when I got home, my mother from Taiwan was in my apartment room.
Expresses contrast or unexpected contradiction (even though..., despite...).
Embeds an interrogative question into a sentence (how...).
Even though I hadn't given her the room key, I had no idea how she got into the room.
have not handed over, have not given
did not know, could not understand
Metaphorical comparison pattern meaning 'just like / as if...', used here to liken the mother's carefree, youthful behavior to that of a high school student.
My mother is just like a high school student.
Receiving a helpful action from someone (having the landlord unlock the room as a favor).
Indirectly quotes what another person said (said that...).
When I asked, she said the landlord had unlocked the room for her.
The suffix 〜たい changes to the て-form to connect clauses and indicate a cause or reason (because [she] wanted to see...).
Pattern used to convey hearsay or information learned from others (I heard that...).
I heard that my mother came to Japan because she wanted to see a Japanese idol's concert.
wanting to see, wanting to watch
Expresses a change or transition into a new state (turning 50 years old).
My mother, who turns 50 this year, is a fan of a 21-year-old idol.
Figurative comparison (like, similar to; as if like a young girl).
Expresses an action moving away from the speaker's location or viewpoint (heading out, going away).
So, she dressed up like a young girl and headed off to the concert.
and so, therefore, because of that
Indicates a starting point in time after doing something (ever since coming to Japan).
Indicates a change in state or ability (learned to cook, became able to cook).
Expresses a desire or wish for someone else to do something (wanting mother to eat one's cooking).
Since I learned how to cook after coming to Japan, I really wanted my mother to eat my food.
Non-exhaustive listing particle connecting nouns (Japanese food, Taiwanese food, etc.).
Describes an action repeated or sustained continuously in the past (was always waiting for mother to return).
So, every evening I cooked Japanese or Taiwanese food and waited for my mother to come home.
Conjunction indicating a strong contrast contrary to expectations (and yet, despite that).
Describes movement directed toward the speaker (returning home).
Even so, my mother came home around midnight every night.
and yet, despite that, even so
Describes performing the subsequent action without doing the prior action (without eating together, ...).
Expresses doing nothing but a certain action or doing it excessively (doing nothing but, always hanging out).
Conjecture based on gathered information or observed evidence (it seems that, I heard that).
Apparently, she did not eat with me even once and spent all her time hanging out with friends.
Used to name or identify a person or thing: 'named...', 'called...'
I have a friend named Emi Watanabe.
to have, there is (for animate beings)
Placed after a quantity to indicate an approximation: 'about...', 'around...'
Past-tense relative clause modifying a noun: the friend whom I 'met'
She is a friend I met at work about 10 years ago.
Used to ask a question politely, gently, or to wonder to oneself ('could it be that...?', 'I wonder...').
Combines the cause marker "〜から" (because) with the expression of conjecture "〜と思います" (I think...), expressing "I think it is because...".
Expresses an ongoing habit, attitude, or continuous state (here, consistently valuing oneself).
I think it is probably because Emi is very honest with herself and values herself very much.
Uses a な-adjective to directly modify the following noun ("honest Emi").
Emphatic particle: (does not lie) even to other people as well.
Emi, who is honest with herself, does not lie to others either.
does not say, not to tell
A relative clause modifying the following noun ("Emi, who cherishes...").
A phrase expressing the action of cherishing, valuing, or taking good care of the mentioned subject.
Emi, who values herself, also cherishes other people.
to cherish, to value, to treasure
to cherish, to value, to treasure
Used to emphasize a reason or provide an explanation for the preceding statement.
Expresses personal thoughts or opinions ("I think that...").
That is why I think everyone likes Emi so much.
Particle meaning "also" or "too", identifying the speaker with the mentioned group.
I am one of them too.
Expresses an objective, polite, and softer reason or cause ("because / since...").
Expresses that an action or event occasionally happens (or does not happen).
Having quit my previous job and now working at another company, there is hardly anything at work that surprises me anymore.
there is not, to not exist
to quit, to leave, to stop
to be surprised, to be startled
Sentence-ending particle used to seek agreement or gently express an exclamation ("right?", "isn't it?").
Connecting te-form of an i-adjective (明るい -> 明るくて) used to link multiple characteristics: 'both... and...'
She is always cheerful and carefree.
Gentle imperative form typically used by a superior to a subordinate: 'do...'
Passive form of 言う combined with the quotation particle と: 'to be told to...'
Even when told by the department manager to submit the report, Emi does not turn it in right away.
even if told, even when told
does not submit, will not hand in
Conditional pattern expressing a natural consequence or habitual reaction: 'whenever...', 'as soon as...'
Whenever she catches a cold, she immediately takes time off from work.
to take time off, to be absent
Pattern expressing comparison or conjecture based on visual impression: 'looks like...', 'seems like...'
She seems like a bad employee, doesn't she?
Connects an action to an inevitable result or realization: 'whenever...', 'when...'
Expresses that something occurs occasionally: 'there are times when...', 'sometimes...'
When watching Emi at work, there are often things that surprise me.
be surprised, be startled, be shocked
Expresses doing something unintentionally, regrettably, or by accident: 'ended up doing', 'blurted out'
Expresses a past experience or that an event occurred in the past: 'there was a time when...', 'have experienced...'
On a hot summer day, when the president smelled a bit, she ended up blurting out, "You smell bad."
ended up saying, accidentally blurted out
Negative potential form in the past tense: 'could not say', 'was unable to say'
Complete negation (何も言えませんでした): 'could not say anything at all'
At that time, I, the other people, and the president were all stunned and couldn't say a word.
could not say, was unable to say
Expresses liking, fondness, or affection toward N: 'like / love N'
Even so, people at the company, clients, and everyone else all love Emi.
love, be very fond of, like very much
Expresses the speaker's desire or wish (wanting to travel).
Indicates the time when an action takes place, meaning 'when / at the time of...'.
Used to list representative actions (going somewhere, doing something, etc.).
When you want to travel to Tochigi Prefecture, where should you go and what should you do to have fun?
first, first of all, to begin with
Particle meaning "also / too", adding culinary appeal alongside hot springs and beautiful scenery.
There are also various delicious foods.
Adverb used to emphasize a prominent or representative item from a whole: 'especially', 'particularly'.
Used for naming or identifying: the noun before という is the specific name of the noun that follows ("a strawberry called Skyberry").
Polite past passive form of つくる (つくられる), expressing that something was developed or created by people.
After that, a large strawberry called "Skyberry" was created.
was made, was created, was produced
Passive continuous form of 使う, expressing a customary state or ongoing situation where something is regularly used for a specific purpose.
Pattern meaning "both A and B...", used to group multiple items that share the same characteristic or action.
Lists representative actions (such as buying, eating) in no particular chronological order.
Pattern expressing potential or ability: "can do V", "be able to do V".
Both "Tochiotome" and "Skyberry" can be bought and eaten in various places across Tochigi Prefecture.
Used for naming or identifying: 'called / named...'.
Indicates the starting point in time: 'from / since (long ago)'.
In Tochigi Prefecture, there are hot springs that have been famous since long ago, called Nasu Hot Spring and Kinugawa Hot Spring.
Expresses a desire or wish (wanting to go).
Expresses the speaker's uncertain conjecture: 'might / may... (about 50% probability)'.
People who like hot springs might want to visit both hot springs in one day.
Indicates an objective, mild reason or cause: 'because / since...'.
Expresses a personal thought or opinion: 'I think that...'.
However, because they are far apart, I think that would be difficult.
Polite invitation or suggestion: 'let's / shall we...'.
Let's stay overnight at just one of the two places.
The next great spot is Lake Chuzenji in autumn.
Indicates a change of state: 'to become / turn into...'.
Pattern expressing ability or possibility: 'can / to be able to do something'.
Particle used for non-exhaustive listing of nouns: 'and, such as...'.
The leaves on the trees around the lake turn red and yellow, and you can see the beautiful autumn foliage.
autumn foliage, autumn colors, red leaves
Conditional pattern indicating a natural consequence: 'whenever / when... then...'.
Uses the te-form to connect actions or states, and to indicate a mild cause or reason.
When you travel across the lake by boat, you can see the scenery clearly and it feels very pleasant.
default.tests.2.skills.0.sections.0.passages.0.s: Going somewhere to do something (indicates the purpose of movement)
I went to an electronics store to buy a rice cooker and an electric kettle.
to buy, in order to buy
There is / to have something (used for inanimate objects)
Noun-modifying clause modifying the following noun
Non-exhaustive listing of nouns ('such as... and...')
Particle indicating a limit of time or scope ('within / in...')
There were rice cookers that can cook rice and side dishes at the same time, and kettles that boil water in 2 seconds.
can do, to be made, to be ready
Sentence-ending particle used to seek agreement or express exclamation ('isn't it?', 'right?')
That is really convenient, isn't it?
Indicates a change of state ('to become...')
Conjunction placed at the beginning of a sentence expressing contrast ('but', 'however')
However, I bought the regular product.
Connective form (て-form) of な-adjectives used to link clauses for listing or stating a reason ('...and...')
Placed at the end of a sentence to state a cause or reason ('because...')
Because I like cooking, and the time spent cooking is enjoyable.
default.tests.2.skills.0.sections.0.passages.1.s: Particle indicating the location where an action takes place or the setting
Sentence pattern indicating the existence of an inanimate object at a location
There is this note on Mr. Mack's desk.
to be, to exist, there is
Throughout a period of time / within the specified time limit for an action
Polite expression used to ask someone to do something
Please take care of the following tasks this morning.
in the morning, during the morning
Particle indicating the means or method of performing an action
Sentence pattern used to politely request or instruct someone to do something
Please do them in the order of 1, 2.
To send something to someone (〜に indicates the recipient)
Particle indicating means or method (by email)
1. Please send the president's message to Mr. Oyama at N Printing by email.
Indicates a resulting state (知っている: to know / have information)
Conjunction expressing reason or cause (because, so)
Mr. Honda knows the email address, so please ask him.
To compile into something (〜に indicates the resulting form/product)
2. Please compile what was discussed in yesterday's meeting into a document.
To send something to someone (〜に indicates the recipient)
Particle indicating means of action (by email)
Please send that to everyone by email.
default.tests.2.skills.0.sections.0.passages.2.s: Indicates the direction or destination of movement (going to a place)
Last week, I went to an art museum.
Expresses the existence or presence of animate beings (people or animals)
There were about 20 junior high school students.
junior high school student, middle school student
Nominalizes a verb (the act of doing something)
Hearsay expression: I heard that... / they say that...
I heard that looking at paintings here is today's lesson.
to see, to look at, to watch
Connects actions in chronological order (sit down and then look)
Expresses a continuous or prolonged action in the past
They sat in front of a painting and looked at it together for a long time.
To explain or give an explanation about N
Expresses an ongoing action at a specific point in the past
The teacher was explaining the paintings.
A plain-form verb precedes and modifies a noun (the picture that [they] are looking at)
The particle も combined with いました indicates 'there were also (people doing something)'
There were also children copying the paintings they were looking at directly into their notebooks.
as is, just as it is
Expresses one's thoughts or feelings in the past (thought that...)
I thought it was a very good lesson.
default.tests.2.skills.0.sections.1.passages.0.s: Noun-modifying clause (the essay that Ryu wrote)
This is an essay written by Ryu.
Negative form of the verb 疲れる (つかれる: to get tired)
The color white does not make you tired.
To feel that..., have a feeling that...
Used to explain a reason or clarify the reality behind a situation.
In reality, it was the same, but I felt that it was heavy.
To convey or express something to someone.
Because of this, I shared my idea with the president of the company where I worked part-time.
Advice or suggestion: Should do something, it is better to do something.
Quoting spoken content: To say that...
Used to explain in detail what was previously mentioned.
I said that it would be better to change the color of the shipping boxes to white.
Explaining a cause: This is because..., the reason is that...
This is because white feels lighter than black or brown.
Non-exhaustive listing of nouns: things like... and...
For example, sports shirts and socks are usually white.
Potential form of Group 1 verbs (動く -> 動ける): can move / able to move.
Conjunctive て-form expressing cause and effect (because it feels light, one can move around a lot).
Used for emphasis or to explain a factual reason.
Because it feels light, one can move around a lot.
Comparison pattern expressing preference: ... is better (here: choosing white is better).
Transforming a な-adjective into an adverb (かんたんに) to modify a verb: can do easily.
I told the president that work could be done more easily if they were white.
Someone does something for one's benefit (expressing gratitude).
The president listened very attentively to what I had to say.
Time suffix: after a period of... (1か月後: after one month).
And then, one month later, the white boxes arrived.
one month later, after one month
Indicates a change of state: 'to become...'. Used with na-adjectives (drop な) + に + なりました (かんたんになりました: became easier).
After that, the work became much easier.
by far, much more, all along
Placed after a plain-form clause to state a reason or cause: 'because...', 'since...'.
Indicates a habit or an action sustained over a period of time in the past: 'used to (play sports)'.
Because I used to play sports, I already knew this.
knew, was aware of (past form of 〜ている)
Particle で indicates means, method, or medium: 'by', 'through', 'via (studying)'.
Polite negative form of a noun: 'is not...', 'are not...'.
This is not something I learned from studying.
knew, learned (past form of 知る)
Lists nouns with the meaning 'whether... or...', 'either... or...'.
Indicates the ability to perform an action: 'can do V' (見つけることができる: can find).
Expresses personal thought or opinion: 'I think that...'.
I think that whether in sports or play, we can find ideas that can be used for work.
can do, to be able to
When, at the time of (indicates a point in time in the past)
Past continuous form, expressing a habit or an action sustained over a period in the past
I have been playing sports since I was a child.
Thought that... (expresses a thought or impression)
Have done before, there are times when (expresses past experience)
There was a time when I thought that was a good thing.
Noun modification: dictionary form verb modifying a noun (carrying job)
When doing something in the past
This is a story from when I was working a part-time job carrying packages.
Not very... (polite past negative of an i-adjective: 重い -> 重くありませんでした)
Those packages were not very heavy.
was not heavy, were not heavy
When it comes to / upon reaching (indicates a point in time leading to a subsequent state)
Te-form connecting clauses to show cause and effect (being tired, so unable to move)
Potential form in past negative (動く -> 動ける -> 動けませんでした: could not move)
However, toward the end of work, I was tired and could barely move.
toward the end, around closing time
To become... (indicates a change of state for an i-adjective: 重い -> 重くなる)
Because... (used to explain a reason or cause)
That is because the packages gradually became heavier.
It is not that... (used to negate or clarify a fact)
However, it didn't actually become heavier.
This is a notice from a Japanese language school.
Pattern used to make a polite request or give advice: Please do...
Expresses an ongoing state of keeping an object in one's possession.
Please keep it with you yourself.
When/at the time of...: Expresses the timing or occasion when an event or situation occurs.
Please do...: Used to make a polite request, instruction, or recommendation.
When your wallet or money is missing, please tell the teacher.
lost, missing (past form of なくなる)
tell, report, say (te-form of 言う)
Expresses movement directed toward the speaker or current space (sneaking inside).
Hearsay pattern expressing information heard from another source: 'I heard that...', 'apparently'.
Apparently, a thief has been entering the school recently.
Non-exhaustive listing of representative nouns (such as..., and so on).
Polite pattern used to ask, request, or advise someone to do something (please do...).
Please always keep important items with you, such as your wallet and money.
Negative verb form used to connect clauses (without doing V / instead of doing V...).
Pattern indicating the time or occasion when an action or state occurs (when / at the time of...).
Even during lunch break or class in the computer room, do not leave it in the classroom, but...
do not put, do not leave behind
Expresses a continuing state or habit; here, indicates the state of living/residing in a place.
A woman lives next door to my house.
Polite negative form of the な-adjective 「好き」, expressing that one does not like something.
That person does not like black cats.
Whenever...; expresses an inevitable consequence: whenever one sees a black cat, bad things happen.
Used to express an ongoing thought or belief of a third person.
She thinks: "If you see a black cat, bad things will happen."
The て-form of い-adjectives, used to connect two qualities (black back and white belly).
My cat is a cat with a black back and a white belly.
Conjunction indicating cause or reason: because, since...
Pattern expressing someone's thoughts or judgments.
However, the woman next door thinks it is a black cat, so she dislikes my cat.
Pattern indicating a point in time: when/at the time of doing something.
The particle に marks the person or target one meets.
When I was outside with my cat, I met that woman.
Polite past negative form of verbs (did not...).
Uses the -te form to connect actions in chronological order (lifted up, then showed).
So, I picked up the cat and showed her its belly.
and then, so, because of that
Connects a sequence of consecutive actions in a sentence.
She looked at the cat's belly and laughed.
Expresses a change of state with na-adjectives (remove な + になる): to become..., to start liking.
She came to like my cat.
came to like, grew fond of
To send N2 to recipient N1 (particle に marks the recipient).
Ai sent a letter to Mayuko.
Expresses the speaker's thoughts or judgment (I think that...)
Sentence-ending particle used to emphasize information or share an opinion with the listener.
I think it will be a lot of fun.
Polite/honorific prefix placed before adjectives or nouns to show courtesy when asking after someone.
healthy, well, in good health (polite form)
From... to... (indicates starting point から and destination に).
A certain period of time has passed since doing action V.
Three months have passed since I moved from Yokohama to Osaka.
moving, relocating (te-form of 引っ越す)
Converts an i-adjective into an adverb to modify the following verb (楽しく働く: to work happily).
Expresses an ongoing state or current occupation.
I am currently enjoying working at a bookstore.
The particle で indicates the reason or purpose of travel (仕事で: for work/on business)
On the 9th of next month, I am going to Yokohama for work.
From... to... (indicates a time span from the 10th to the 12th)
Used to explain background context or provide new information to the listener
Near Yokohama Station, there is a big bookstore event taking place from the 10th to the 12th.
to be held, to take place, there is
Expresses preference or liking something (used with the particle が)
..., right? / ..., isn't it? (used to confirm information and seek agreement)
You like books, don't you, Mayuko?
Because..., since... (indicates a reason or cause in a polite, gentle manner)
Passive voice (受身形) of Group 1 verbs (売る → 売られる: to be sold)
I think that... (expresses personal opinion or judgment)
Since many different bookstores are participating in this event, I think lots of interesting things will be sold.
To come in order to do something (indicates the purpose of movement)
Won't you...? / Would you like to...? (polite invitation to do something together)
If you'd like, would you like to come see it?
if you like, if it's okay
to see, to watch, to look at
won't you come?, would you like to come?
Used to name or define a noun: "called ~", "known as ~".
There is a term called "morning activities" (asakatsu).
morning activity, morning routine (waking up early to study, exercise, etc.)
Indicates a time reference: "before doing something / before N".
Lists representative examples of things or actions: "such as ~, and so on".
Nominalizes a verb to explain or define: "the act of ~, doing ~".
This refers to waking up early in the morning and using the time before going to school or work for hobbies, studying, sports, and other activities.
Lists representative actions: "doing things like ~ and ~".
Lists parallel clauses or facts: "both... and...", "not only... but also...".
Expresses hearsay or an inference: "I hear that ~", "it seems that ~".
Apparently, some people read books at coffee shops or study in study groups, while others go running.
to exist, to be (for animate beings)
Expresses a desire to try doing something: "want to try doing ~".
Expresses the speaker's thoughts or intentions: "to think that ~".
Asks for advice or a course of action: "should I ~?", "what should one do?".
I also thought I would like to try morning activities, but I don't really know what I should do.
to think, thought (as in 思いました)
Connects clauses to list multiple reasons: "not only because..., but also...".
Placed at the end of a sentence to explain or emphasize the reason: "it is because ~".
It is because I'm currently injured so I can't play sports, and besides, my hobby is sleeping.
being injured, having an injury, doing
to sleep, to go to bed, to lie down

Even if / even though... (expresses concession: even though she waited 10 days, the goods did not arrive).
Because / since... (states an objective cause or reason leading to the action of calling).
However, even after waiting 10 days, the goods did not arrive, so she called that tea company.
The て form of a noun used to connect clauses, indicating a cause or state ('because they are away...').
Cannot do something (negative potential form of the Group 3 verb 連絡する).
However, they were always away (no one answered), so she could not get in touch.
absence, being away from home, unattended
Suffered an unfortunate action (combination of the passive form 〜られる and 〜てしまう expressing regret or an undesirable outcome).
Saying that... (used to directly quote speech).
Be... -ing (expresses an ongoing emotional state of anger)
My mother said, "My money was taken!" and is very angry.
Particle meaning 'also' or 'too' (my mother is also...).
My mother is one of them.
Indicates the time or occasion an action takes place: 'when...' or 'while...'.
Passive form of 言う, indicating being told something by someone else.
While walking around town, my mother was addressed by an unfamiliar man: "Excuse me ma'am, do you have a moment?"
a moment, a little, excuse me
was told, was addressed, was asked
Connects sequential actions meaning 'when... then...' (when she asked, the person spoke).
Indicates judgment based on appearance: 'looks like...', 'seems...' (お元気そう).
Expresses purpose: 'in order to...', 'so as to...' (in order to stay healthy).

When my mother asked, "What is it?", that person said to her very politely, "You look very healthy, ma'am, but to keep staying healthy from now on, it would be very good for you to drink this every day."
to be, to stay, to remain
Then, that person introduced a tea called "Kenko Tea".
Conjunction connecting two contrasting clauses meaning 'although...', 'but...'.
Indicates conjecture based on impression: 'seems...', 'looks like...' (よさそう).
Expresses personal opinion or thought: 'to think that...', 'to consider that...'.
Hearing the man's explanation, my mother thought that although the tea was not cheap, it seemed truly good for her health.
Expresses a personal decision: 'to decide to do something'.
Therefore, my mother decided to buy the tea.
and so, therefore, because of that
Indicates a time limit: 'within / by the end of' (here, within this week).
Grammar pattern used to directly quote speech: 'to say that...'.
"The goods will arrive at your home within this week," the man said.
within this week, by the end of this week
Expresses a sequence of actions: 'after doing V1, do V2'.
After parting ways with the man, my mother sent the money.
to part ways, to leave, to separate
default.tests.3.skills.0.sections.1.passages.1.s: Whenever/when... then... (expresses a habit or an inevitable consequence following an action or event)
Wondering to oneself what to do (wondering where to go)
Whenever a vacation approaches, I think about where to go.
Listing representative items or actions (such as ..., among others)
Both ... and ... (emphasizes that both share the same trait)
Different from ... (comparing differences with an entity)
Unusual food, flowers and trees seen for the first time, accents heard for the first time—both nature and culture are vastly different from where I live.
to see, to look, to watch
To try doing something (考えてみる: to try thinking about it)
To have done something before (expresses past experience)
When I think about it, even within my own country, the places I have been to are few, and the places I don't know are far more numerous.
come to think of it, when you think about it
Want to do V (expresses one's own desire or wish)
Therefore, before spending a lot of time and money traveling abroad, I first want to get to know my own country well.
Connects actions in chronological order (after returning from Okinawa...)
To come to, to start to... (expresses a change in mindset or habit)
After returning from Okinawa, I began to think that way.
to return, to go back, to come home
N for the purpose of V (a trip to learn about...)
Planning to do something (expresses an intention formed beforehand and still ongoing)
From now on, I plan to travel to learn more about my own country.
to know, to learn about, to find out
planning to do, intending to do
Listing representative actions (doing things like traveling by bicycle and staying at friends' houses)
Having someone do something / receiving a favor (having a friend let one stay over)
When I was a student, since I didn't have money, I traveled by bicycle and stayed over at friends' houses.
did not have, there was not
being allowed to stay over, being put up, etc.
Had long wanted to do something over an extended period in the past
Non-exhaustive listing of nouns (such as... and...)
However, I had always wanted to go abroad, especially hoping to visit America or Europe.
Connecting actions sequentially in chronological order (working a part-time job and then going to America)
Before a certain event or point in time
So I worked a part-time job and went to America before graduating.
Only, just (indicates an exclusive limit to that specific scope or occasion)
But that was the only time I traveled abroad.
B is more... than A (comparative pattern)
Ever since I started working at the company this spring, the issue of time has become bigger than the issue of money.
starting to work, beginning to work
Potential form: expresses the ability or inability to perform an action (とれない: cannot take time off)
Because..., since... (states a cause or reason)
Because I cannot take long holidays, traveling abroad is still difficult as expected.
cannot take (time off), unable to obtain
Conjunction expressing a result: therefore, because of that, so
Therefore, during the May holiday, I went to Okinawa.
On this trip, I had a precious experience.
default.tests.3.skills.0.sections.1.passages.2.s: Expresses an occupation, habit, or continuous state (here, growing vegetables as an occupation).
Mr. Kawakami is growing vegetables in a town near Tokyo.
to grow, to make, to produce
When, at the time of (indicates the point in time an event occurs).
To become (change of state or occupation).
Expresses a desire or wish held continuously over a period of time in the past.
When he was young, Mr. Kawakami wanted to become a singer.
Particle meaning "also / even", emphasizing that even people from restaurants in Tokyo come to buy.
Indicates the purpose of movement (to come to do something). In the sentence, 「買いに来ます」 means "come to buy".
Even people from restaurants in Tokyo come to buy.
Conjunction connecting two clauses for contrast ('...while...', '...but...').
While... (two actions occurring simultaneously, with the latter being the main focus).
His parents grew vegetables in a large field, while Mr. Kawakami was working a part-time job in Tokyo and studying singing.
to grow, to make, to produce
Particle で indicating a cause or reason leading to an outcome (passing away due to an accident).
When he was 25 years old, his parents passed away in an accident.
Expresses one's intention or plan to do something ('intend to...', 'thinking of doing...').
Noun-modifying clause: 「両親が野菜を作っていた畑」 (the field where his parents used to grow vegetables).
Mr. Kawakami thought of selling the field where his parents used to grow vegetables.
Conditional pattern 'if... then...' (if this place is sold...).
Expresses an unintended action with a sense of regret ('houses will end up being built').
Expresses a desire for someone not to do something ('want you not to...', 'please don't...').

Then, a neighbor came over and said, "This is no ordinary field. It has rich soil that your parents built up. If you sell this place, houses will probably end up being built here. I want you not to sell this field."
to exist, there is, to have
Doing the subsequent action without doing the preceding action ('growing vegetables without using pesticides').
Someone does something that brings joy or benefit to the speaker or the speaker's in-group.
Nominalizing a clause with の ('remembering that father once said...').
Mr. Kawakami recalled his father saying, "Vegetables grown without chemicals don't look good. But everyone is delighted, saying they are delicious and good for their health."
Causes or allows someone to feel an emotion or perform an action (人を喜ばせる: to make people happy).
Expresses a gradual change in perception or habit ('gradually realize...', 'come to think that...').
Nominalizes a verb to create a noun phrase that functions as the subject or predicate in a sentence.
Mr. Kawakami wanted to do work that made people happy, and he came to realize that growing delicious vegetables was also a way to bring joy to people.
to please, to make happy, to delight
to make, to grow, to produce
Connects two sequential actions occurring in chronological order ('quit... and then started...').
To start or begin performing an action or activity.
And then, ④ he gave up studying singing and started growing vegetables.
Connects adjectives to list parallel qualities ('both delicious and good').
Expresses an objective, polite reason or cause ('because...', 'since...').
Phrase meaning to be popular or well-liked by many people.
Now, the vegetables grown by Mr. Kawakami are delicious and good for one's health, so they are very popular.
to exist, to have, to be
Indicates that an event or activity takes place at a location.
This coming Saturday, there will be a party at Professor Kobayashi's house.
To go to do something (indicates the purpose of movement).
Together with someone (doing an action together).
So, I went to the department store with Jimmy to buy a souvenir.
to buy, in order to buy
Should one do / asking for advice or wondering what to do.
Expresses that an action happened unintentionally, or carries a sense of regret or trouble.
There were so many things I wanted at the department store that I was at a loss as to what to buy.
to exist, to have, there is
was troubled, ended up at a loss
Used after a numeral or counter to indicate an approximate amount.
The budget is about 1,000 yen per person.
Too... (exceeding normal limits, expresses dissatisfaction or complaint).
I found some beautiful scarves, but they were all too expensive.
In the end, I bought a wine glass.
in the end, after all, eventually
I think ... probably (expresses personal conjecture about something).
Indicates a change in state or emotion (to become...).
It was more expensive than 1,000 yen, but thinking that my teacher, who likes alcohol, would surely like it made me happy.
to like, to be pleased with
when thinking that, at the thought that
Expresses the existence or location of inanimate objects or places at a specific location (in Chiba).
Expresses an ongoing state or habitual lifestyle (living).
Currently, I live in a house located in Chiba.
to be, to exist, to be located
Noun-modifying relative clause (the person 'living in this house').
The people living in this house are all from the same company.
Non-exhaustive listing of representative nouns (such as..., etc.)
Generalizes an action or topic (matters concerning..., things about...)
In the beginning, I struggled a lot with things like the language and meals.
Nominalizes a verb to serve as the subject or topic in a sentence (the act of taking a bath...)
Conjugating an い-adjective into its て-form to connect adjectives or indicate a cause (being embarrassed, so...)
Taking a bath together with everyone was also embarrassing and unpleasant for me.
To get used to something or an environment (paired with the particle に)
To become close friends with someone, to get along well with someone
Expresses an objective and polite reason or cause (because..., so...)
But now I have completely gotten used to life in the dormitory and become good friends with everyone; since I am good at cooking, on my days off I often treat my dorm friends to a meal.
treat someone to a meal, host
Conjunction indicating a result that follows directly after a preceding action
Expresses the observable emotion or reaction of a third person (everyone is looking very pleased)
When I do, everyone is very delighted.
That is what makes me happiest.
To have an interest or passion in something (used with particle に)
Grammar pattern expressing past experience: have never done (an action) before
Nominalizing a verb using の to express preference (to like doing something)
Ever since I was a child, I have been interested in many different things, and I like doing things that I have never done before.
childhood, when one was a child
Conjunction indicating cause and effect (and so, that is why, therefore)
The particle の replaces が in a relative clause modifying a noun (興味のあった日本)
Used to explain the reason, background, or cause behind a situation
That is why I came to Japan, a place I had already been interested in for a long time.
and so, because of that, therefore
Nominalizes a verb (V-る + こと: watching movies)
Potential form of Group 2 verbs (見られます: can watch, able to watch)
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrasting meaning (but, however)
Nowadays, with the internet, DVDs, and the like, you can easily watch them at home, but I always watch them at the movie theater.
and so on, and the like, etc.
can see, can watch, be able to watch
Superlative pattern within a scope or category (the most... among/out of...)
Pattern nominalizing the preceding clause to emphasize the topic or focus (the one that... is... / what... is...)
Out of all the movies I have seen so far, the best one was 「Neko Samurai」.
until now, so far, up to now
Recently, I watched the movie 「A Kitten's Story」.
Expresses a third person's desire (見たがっていた: wanted to see)
Judgment based on appearance (おもしろそう: looks interesting/fun)
Indicates the purpose of movement (見に行く: go to see)
Last Sunday, my friend really wanted to see that movie, so even though I didn't think it looked very interesting, I went to watch it.
wanted to see, wanted to watch
went to see, went to watch
Comparative pattern meaning 'more than' (思っていたより: more than I thought)
However, it was much better than I had expected.
Connects い-adjectives to list characteristics (かわいくて: cute and...)
The kittens were cute, and the mountain scenery was also very beautiful.
Pattern expressing similarity ('just like...', 'in the same way as...')
Expresses a state of possession (持っている: have, possess)
To realize or come to understand a fact or situation
I was deeply moved to realize that cat parents and their kittens also have affection, just like human parents and children.
similarly, in the same way, just like
Expresses a desire for someone else to perform an action (wanting everyone to see)
Used to express personal thoughts or opinions ('I think that...').
I think I want everyone to see this movie too.
want (someone) to see, want (someone) to watch
The te-form (connective form) of na-adjectives (大好きで), used to connect clauses meaning 'and' or 'because / so'.
Pattern indicating the frequency of an action within a specific time period (1か月に2、3回: two to three times a month).
I love karaoke, and I go to karaoke with friends two or three times a month.
two or three times, a few times
Follows a point in time or age to mean 'around' or 'about' (二十歳ごろ: around the age of twenty).
Nominalizes a verb to function as an object or subject (歌うの: singing / the act of singing).
Concessive conditional pattern meaning 'even if / even though' (飲みに行っても: even if going out drinking).
Actually, until around the age of twenty, I hated singing in front of people, and even when I went out drinking with friends, I did not sing at all.
actually, as a matter of fact, to tell the truth
in front of people, in public
not at all, entirely not (used with negative)
Connects two actions or states in chronological order (飲んで、...になりました: drank and then became...).
Indicates a change of state (楽しい気分になりました: got into a cheerful mood).
One day, I drank a lot of alcohol and felt very happy.
Describes an action taking place while in a certain ongoing state (酔っている時に: while being drunk / when intoxicated).
Used to express that an action leads to a subsequent unexpected result or discovery (歌を歌ったら...もらいました: after/upon singing, received applause).
To receive something from someone (みんなから大きな拍手をもらいました: received a big round of applause from everyone).
When I was drunk, I just sang whatever song came to mind, and I received a big round of applause from everyone.
time, when, at the time of
Negative form of a na-adjective combined with なる, expressing a change in state (嫌いじゃなくなり: no longer disliking / ceased to dislike).
Indicates a gradual change progressing up to the present moment (好きになってきました: have gradually come to like).
From that point on, I no longer disliked karaoke and gradually grew to love it.
Indicates the point in time after an action has been completed (飲んだ時: when/after having drunk).
Indicates limitation: 'only', 'just' (飲んだ時だけ: only when having drunk alcohol).
Expresses that an action or habit rarely or never happens (歌うことはほとんどありません: hardly ever sing).
In Japan, I only sang when I drank alcohol, but in Taiwan where I live now, I rarely drink and sing.
does not happen, there is no
Expresses two simultaneous actions: 'while doing...' (飲みながら歌う: singing while drinking).
Conditional sentence pattern 'if... then' (上手に歌いたいなら: if you want to sing well).
Combination of advice and a shift in mindset: '飲まないで歌ったほうがいい' (should sing without drinking alcohol) + '〜と思うようになりました' (started to think that...).
At first, singing while drinking tea felt strange, but now I have come to think that if you want to sing well, it is better to sing without drinking alcohol.
at first, in the beginning, early on
Speaking of / When mentioning N (introduces a representative, typical topic)
Speaking of pets, many people probably keep dogs or cats.
As / in the role of (keeping as a pet)
Relative clause modifying the following noun (a company I know)
The president of a company I know keeps several snakes as pets.
Expresses concession or extension of scope: "even in... / even if...".
Expresses ability or possibility: "can do something" (here: can be kept/raised).
In addition, you can keep them even in small spaces.
to keep (a pet), to raise (an animal)
Verb stem (ます-form without ます) combined with やすい expresses that something is "easy to do" (飼いやすい: easy to keep).
Used to indirectly quote a third person's words, thoughts, or opinions: "says that...".
In this way, he says that snakes are very good because they are easy to keep.
in this way, like this, thus
easy to keep and, easy to raise and
Ever since doing V / After doing V
I hear it has already been about 15 or 16 years since he started keeping them.
starting to keep, starting to raise
Connecting clauses to express a sequence of consecutive actions
Place / spot to do V (sleeping place)
I hear that...; It is said that... (reporting hearsay)
I hear that he keeps snakes in his house, laying out a futon in a small room to make a sleeping place for the snakes.
Does not do things like... (listing representative actions)
...and also...; not only... but also... (listing reasons)
Because..., since... (stating a cause or reason objectively)
I hear that that snake is safe because it doesn't bite people, and it also has no venom.
To become, change of state (e.g., to grow big/grow up)
Never happens / It is never the case that... (no occurrence of V)
Because his daughter also grew up with snakes, I hear she never feels scared of them.
big, large, greatly (growing up, becoming big)
Total affirmation (どの〜にも: every single...)
To be named / to have a name (intransitive verb indicating state)
Every snake is given a name such as "Mimi" or "Nono".
Indicating cause or reason (for various reasons)
Easy to do V (easy to keep/raise)
I hear that...; It is said that... (reporting hearsay)
I hear that snakes are easy to keep for various reasons.
easy to keep, easy to raise
Frequency of an action (e.g., once a week)
Indicates that something is acceptable or sufficient: "... is fine / ... will do"
Even if / even though one does V... (e.g., it is fine even if one goes out)
First of all, feeding them about once a week is enough, so it's fine even if the whole family goes away on a trip.
first of all, to begin with, first
Like N, as N (comparison of similarity: like a dog)
Also no need to do V / does not do V either, there is no doing V
To cause trouble, to bother others
Furthermore, since they do not bark "woof-woof" like dogs, they do not cause trouble for the neighbors.
Indicates doing an action to excess, leading to an undesirable result (in this context, overworking or studying too hard resulting in fatigue).
Lists representative states or actions (when feeling tired, when lacking energy, etc.).
Gives advice or instructions to the reader on what to do (please drink).
Please drink this nutritional drink「Haruka」when you are tired from overworking or overstudying, lacking energy, or when your body somehow feels sluggish and heavy from morning.
etc., and so on, and the like
Relative clause modifying the following noun (運転をするトラック運転手: truck drivers who drive).
Particle meaning 'also for / also to...', indicating an additional beneficiary or recipient.
In addition, this energy drink is also very good for long-distance truck drivers and taxi drivers.
Causative verb (飲ませる) expressing letting or making someone drink.
Polite negative request or prohibition meaning 'please do not do...'
However, please do not let anyone aged 15 or under drink this energy drink.
15 years old and under, aged 15 or under
...years old and under, aged... or younger
please do not let drink, please do not give to drink
Indicates a range 'from... to...' (from 7 years old to 15 years old).
Humble polite expression (お + noun/verb stem + します) used to offer advice or a recommendation to a customer.
For children aged 7 to 15, we recommend the energy drink 「Ayase」.
Connects actions in chronological order or expresses cause and effect.
The particle に is used with the verb 乗る to indicate the vehicle being boarded or ridden.
Last Saturday, our school had a field trip, and we boarded a boat from Hamamatsucho and traveled down the Sumida River.
to be held, to have, to take place
to ride, to board, to get on
Adds の after a dictionary-form verb (乗る) to nominalize the action into 'riding a boat'.
Follows a point in time to indicate a starting point ('since...', 'from...').
Ever since I was a child, I have loved riding boats.
The past-tense verb 生まれた directly modifies the noun 町 ('the town where I was born').
Uses で to connect two nominal clauses ('is Cologne, and...').
The town where I was born is Cologne in Germany, located beside the Rhine River.
A spontaneous verb indicating that a sound reaches one's ears naturally without intentional listening.
The repeated particle も lists multiple elements in parallel ('both hearing birds and the scenery being beautiful').
A conjunction used to connect clauses and transition the narrative smoothly.
When I was a child, I often went down the Rhine River by boat with my family; I could hear birds singing, and the natural scenery was beautiful.
Expresses a wish or desire that continued over a period of time in the past ('had been wanting to...').
Conditional/sequential pattern: upon taking the action in the preceding clause (今思うと - 'thinking back on it now'), one realizes what follows in the subsequent clause.
Expresses one's personal view, thought, or opinion ('I think that...', 'in my opinion...').
Back then, I wanted to live in a bigger town, but looking back now, I think my hometown is truly a wonderful place.
Used with a negative verb to emphasize an exclusive limit, meaning 'only' or 'nothing but' ('could only see old buildings').
Spontaneous potential verb indicating that something comes into view naturally without intentionally looking for it.
Adverb paired with a negative predicate to denote a mild degree: 'not very...', 'not particularly...' ('not very pretty').
On this Sumida River cruise, I could only see old buildings, and the scenery was not very pretty either.
Sumida River boat cruise, going down the Sumida River
The preceding clause in the -te form (聞こえなくて) expresses the cause or reason leading to the emotional state in the subsequent clause (がっかりしました).
Sentence-initial conjunction used to add further information or continue a thought ('moreover, furthermore, in addition').
Moreover, I couldn't hear the birds singing either, which was a bit disappointing.
Each, at a time (indicates an equal distribution of quantity: every 3 months / 3 months each).
To be divided into ~, to split into ~
In Japan, a year is divided into four seasons of three months each.
Throughout, all through (a time period: throughout 1 year)
Listing representative actions or states (e.g., there are days..., there are places...)

In the past, neither the heat nor the cold was very severe throughout the year, but recently Japan has become one of those countries with a large difference between hot and cold days, with summer temperatures in Saitama Prefecture exceeding 42 degrees on some days, and winter temperatures dropping below minus 30 degrees in parts of Hokkaido.
Because of, due to ~ (indicates an objective cause/reason leading to the result in the following clause)
There are times when ~, occasionally ~ happens
Furthermore, because a mountain range lies in the center of Honshu, the weather between the Pacific Ocean side and the Sea of Japan side is sometimes completely different.
to be, to exist, to be located
Even though, although, despite (expresses contrast or contradiction between two clauses)
Only ~ (emphasizes a small quantity or limited extent: differing by only several tens of kilometers)
I heard that ~, it is said that ~ (used to convey hearsay or reported information)

Especially in winter, while heavy snow falls in Niigata Prefecture on the Sea of Japan side, neighboring Gunma Prefecture has fine weather; it is said that places with completely different weather just a few dozen kilometers apart like this are rare even in the world.
like this, in this way, thus
several tens of kilometers, dozens of kilometers
to exist, to be, to have
Even after doing V, the subsequent action or state still continues
Expresses a prolonged, stable state of living or residing
Even after graduating from university, I have continued living here in Tokyo.
Pattern expressing purpose: 'in order to do something'
To go somewhere, perform an action, and then return
The other day, for the first time in a long time, I took a trip to visit a friend from my university days.
the other day, a few days ago
after a long time, for the first time in a while
Provides an example or comparison: 'like...', 'such as...'
Lists characteristics or reasons of a similar nature
Lists representative examples: 'things like...', 'and so on'
The place where my friend is living now is a place that has no trains like in Tokyo, nor things like department stores.
Expresses one's own thought or opinion: 'think that...'
Indirect quotation of what someone said: 'said that...'
I thought it was an inconvenient place, but my friend said they liked that town better than Tokyo.
Passive voice: 'to be cherished, to be valued'
Explains a cause or reason: 'it is because...'
Conveys hearsay or reported information: 'I heard that...'
I heard it is because old buildings and traditional things are cherished there.
Conjunctive form (て-form) of な-adjectives to link characteristics: 'both convenient and...'
Expresses preference or liking: 'to like something'
As for me, I like Tokyo because transportation is convenient and there are many interesting things.
Expresses a reason or cause objectively and politely: 'because...', 'since...'
Indicates movement toward the speaker's current location: 'moved here from the countryside'
Of course, since I moved here from the countryside, I also know the good things about the countryside very well.
have come from, have moved from
Indicates the point in time when an event occurs ('when / back when in 5th grade')
Expresses an ongoing emotional state or condition continuing in the past ('was looking forward to')
Nominalizes an action ('sleeping overnight / doing something for the first time')

When I was in 5th grade of elementary school, I went on a 3-day, 2-night camping trip for the first time through a youth group activity; it was my first time sleeping overnight with friends away from my parents, so I had been looking forward to it very much even before going.
away from, being apart from, separated
to sleep, to go to bed
Lists items concurrently with the meaning 'both... and...' or 'neither... nor...'
Indicates cause or reason ('because / since it is a place...')
Expresses obligation or necessity: must do, have to do ('must prepare by ourselves')
Since neither dad nor mom was there, of course we had to prepare our meals by ourselves.
not be present, not be there, absent
Lists representative actions among others ('doing things like cutting vegetables...')
Indicates the means or method of performing an action ('using wood gathered by ourselves')
We cut vegetables, and we also lit the fire using wood we gathered ourselves.
Lists representative actions among others (doing things like cooking rice, making food...)
And there, we did things like cooking rice and preparing meals.
Expresses past experience of having done something (having helped mother before)
Conjunction indicating contrast between two clauses (although..., but...)
As for cooking, I had helped my mother at home before, but doing it at camp was completely different and took a lot of time.
Lists multiple reasons or states (both hot... and eyes hurting...)
Expresses a change of state for い-adjectives (to become painful/sore)
Nominalizes a clause to function as the subject (the act of cooking...)
On top of that, cooking near the fire was hot, the smoke made my eyes hurt as well, and it was really tough.
to start hurting, to become painful
However, the food we made all by ourselves was very delicious.
Used to explain or name a thing or activity (called 'campfire')
Lists representative actions (such as singing, playing games, performing plays...)
Expresses a change into a result (became a memory)

In the evening, there was an activity called a "campfire" where everyone gathered around a big fire, sang songs, played games, and performed short plays for one another, and this also became an unforgettable memory.
to have, to exist, there is
Connects clauses to express contrast or background/concession (although it was fun...)
Suffering passive voice indicating annoyance or trouble (being bitten by mosquitoes)
The campfire was fun, but at night I got bitten by mosquitoes on both my hands and feet, which was also quite tough.
Indicates something that occurred in the past with a concessive nuance ("although there were times when..., but...")
Connects sequential actions in chronological order ("after finishing, ...")
To feel as though..., to have the feeling that... ("felt like having grown up")
Although there were various difficulties, after camp ended, I felt as though I had grown up a little.
The other day, I bought a new smartphone.
the other day, a few days ago
Indicates a change in state ("started running out of battery quickly")
Used to list multiple reasons or causes ("both because the battery ran out quickly and because the contract ended")
Expresses a decision made by the speaker ("deciding to replace the phone")
My old smartphone was still usable, but the battery started draining quickly, and since my contract renewal date had just arrived, I decided to replace it.
to run out, to be depleted

An i-adjective changes to 〜くなる to express a change of state ('to become high / to rise').
