When the temperature rises, there is one more thing to be careful about.
to be careful, to pay attention, to watch out
Negative conditional pattern 'if not...', used to warn of negative consequences if an action is not taken.
Negative form of a verb combined with 〜くなる, expressing the state of 'no longer (able to)...' (the fever will no longer go down).
Expresses an unfortunate or unintended outcome (developing a fever that will not go down).
If you do not drink enough water, you will get a high fever that will not go down.
Non-exhaustive listing of representative nouns, meaning 'such as... and... and so on'.
Pattern used to give advice or make a polite request ('please drink...').
People who work outdoors or play sports, please drink water, tea, and the like.
etc., and so on, and the like
Pattern expressing permission or acceptance of an alternative ('...is also fine').
Indicates a sequence of actions: doing action B after finishing action A ('after doing...', 'once...').
Indicates making an effort or trying to establish a habit ('make sure to...', 'try to...').
Please make sure to put groceries into the refrigerator right after shopping, and eat food right after cooking.
Indicates making an effort or taking care not to do something ('try not to...', 'make sure not to...').
Please make sure not to eat items that have become old.
Nominalizes a verb to form a noun phrase acting as a subject ('doing... / the act of doing...').
In addition, washing your hands is also important.
and then, after that, in addition
Indicates a temporal condition or sequence ('after returning home, then...').
Sentence pattern used to invite or suggest doing an action together ('let's...').
When you return home from outside, be sure to wash your hands.
Expresses an action occurring before a specific point in time or another action ('before doing...').
Of course, please wash your hands before cooking as well.
Conveys a negative limitation ('with only... it is not enough/won't do').
Washing with just water is not enough.
Connects sequential actions or indicates the means/method for performing the subsequent action ('do... and then...').
Indicates the extent or limit reached ('up to...', 'as far as...', 'even...').
Please use soap and wash thoroughly, even between your fingers.
Expresses an effort to prevent an undesirable outcome ('to make sure not to...', 'so as not to...').
Indicates the purpose or objective of an action ('in order to...', 'for the purpose of...').
This is important in order to ② avoid getting an upset stomach.
to not upset one's stomach, to not get a stomachache
default.tests.4.skills.0.sections.1.passages.1.s: Used to identify or name a thing or concept ('called...', 'named...').
Honorific form of "知っていますか" ('Do you know...?').
Do you know the word "sekiji" (seating order)?
knowing, aware (honorific form of 知っている)
Used to name, define, or quote the content of the following noun (buttons labeled "Open / Close").
In an elevator, the area near the destination buttons or the door "Open / Close" buttons is the lower seating position.
Lists cases with the meaning "whether... or...".
Humble form of 〜てもらう, showing respect when receiving an action from someone of higher status.
Sentence pattern encouraging or urging people to make an effort to do something ("let's make sure to...", "let's try to...").
Whether taking a taxi or an elevator, let us have teachers, seniors, or guests get on first and get off first.
The seat next to the driver's seat in a taxi or the space in front of the elevator buttons has a similar meaning to the area near the room's entrance.
to exist, to have, to be
Modifies the following noun, meaning "that..." / "the idea that..." (e.g., the idea that guests sit far from the entrance).
Conjunction connecting two clauses to express contrast ("...but...").
The idea that guests should sit far from the entrance is useful, but how the guest actually feels is truly the most important thing.
to be useful, to be helpful
actually, in reality, to tell the truth
Expresses two concurrent actions performed by the same subject ("while doing...").
Indicates that an action is easy to do ("easy to...").
If that person says they want to dine while looking at a beautiful garden at a restaurant, let us seat them at a spot where it is easy to see outside, even if it is close to the entrance.
Embedding question clauses into a sentence ('which... or which...').
Pattern used to explain a definition or meaning ('it means that...').
It means which seat is the best, and which seats are second or third.
Connects actions in chronological sequence ("entered the room, and then...")
Embedded question within a sentence (who sits where)
Expresses that an event occurs occasionally or from time to time
When entering a room, sometimes we are troubled over who should sit where.
entering, going into (te-form of 入る)
to be troubled, to be at a loss, to have difficulty
Receiving an action from someone / having or asking someone to do something for you
Proposes an invitation or suggestion to do something together ("let's...")
Let's invite older people—such as teachers and seniors—as well as guests, to sit in places far from the room's entrance.
Doing something in advance as preparation (here, keeping in mind beforehand)
Makes a polite request or instruction ("please...")
Please keep in mind that the places far from the entrance are seats reserved for guests.
to remember, to memorize (て-form of 覚える)
Making an effort to do something, or establishing it as a rule/habit
Conversely, near the entrance, arrange for family members (those who are not guests) or younger people to sit.
and so on, etc., such as
to sit, to take a seat
Lists representative actions ("such as serving tea and snacks...")
Indicates the time an action occurs ("when, at the time of...")
Comparison structure emphasizing a choice ("the closer side/position is more...")
When doing things like serving tea and snacks to guests, sitting closer to the entrance is more convenient.
To board or ride a vehicle (used with the particle に)
When, at the time an action is performed
Particle meaning "also" (emphasizing that seating etiquette applies in taxis and elevators as well as in a room)
When riding in a taxi or an elevator, there is also a seating order.
Indicates the context or scope where an event takes place ("in a taxi...")
In a taxi, the seat next to the driver's seat is the lowest in the seating hierarchy.
default.tests.4.skills.0.sections.1.passages.2.s: When / at the time of doing something (used to connect time clauses).
Polite question ending expressing gentle curiosity or wondering.
When speaking on the phone, why do people say 「もしもし」 (hello)?
Indicates a change of state or habit (to reach the point of being used, to come to be used).
In the sense of..., with the meaning of...
It is said that..., people say that... (conveys general consensus or widely accepted belief).
It is said that this was shortened from 「もうしあげます、もうしあげます」 ("I humbly speak"), meaning "I will speak now," around the time telephones first came into use.
it is said, is said to be
Polite advice/request pattern: please try not to... / please be sure not to...
Expresses hesitation when shifting focus: I would like to say... but... / was about to say... but...
Expressing meaning: also means... / also has the meaning of...

I would like to tell you to please try not to say "moshi moshi" starting today, but this phrase, which was born along with the telephone, also carries the meanings of "Can you hear me?" and "I can hear you."
Pattern granting permission: may do... / it is okay to...
Pattern for politely expressing an opinion or soft judgment: isn't it...? / wouldn't it be...?
Wouldn't it be fine to use it on the phone with someone whose voice you recognize, or with the elderly?
Advises against doing something: had better not, should not (here: should not say).
Indicates a gradual change or continuation from the past up to the present (has been increasing).
However, recently the number of people who think it is better not to say 「もしもし」 has been increasing.
When / at the time an action has occurred.
To try doing something (used here in the volitional form ましょう: let's try doing).
Let us consider what happens when making a phone call to a company.
let's think about, let us consider
Assuming that, suppose that (in the form たとします: hypothesizing a situation that has occurred).
Suppose the person who answered the phone says, 「はい、もしもし」 ("Yes, hello").
Embedded question with a question word: not knowing (where the call connected).
Clause indicating cause or reason (because..., since...).
Indicates a change of state (to become worried).
If you do so, the caller will become worried because they do not know where their call has connected.
if so, in that case, then
Pattern indicating obligation or necessity: must do, have to do.
Therefore, the caller has to ask, 「もしもし、○○商事さんですか」 ('Hello, is this OO Trading?').
Negates the preceding element: not A (but B), instead of A.
Proposes a hypothetical scenario or suggestion for reflection: 'What if...?' / 'How about if...?'
So what if, from the very beginning, instead of saying 「もしもし」, they said, 「はい、○○商事です」 ('Yes, this is OO Trading')?
how about, how would it be, what do you think
Indicates ability or possibility: can do, to be able to perform an action (can start the conversation).
Compound verb: to start doing something (話（を）始める: to start a conversation).
The caller can immediately state their name by saying 「△△ですが」 ('This is △△') and begin the conversation right away.
can do, to be able to
Causative form: to make or let someone do something (in this context, making them practice).
There are times when... / sometimes (something) happens.
Pattern for reporting hearsay/indirect information: I heard that... / it is said that...
It is said that some companies even make people who have newly joined and started working practice not saying 「もしもし」.
to start working, to begin working
to make (someone do), to let (someone do)
default.tests.5.skills.0.sections.0.passages.0.s: Passive form of the verb (つくられる: to be made/built), used to describe how the houses were constructed.
Used for non-exhaustive listing of nouns (windows, entrances, etc.).
Converts an い-adjective into an adverb (大きく: in a large way / largely) to modify the following verb.
Japanese houses used to be built with large windows and entrances.
Expresses an objective cause or reason (because summer is hot...).
Placed at the end of a sentence to explain the reason for the preceding statement (it is because...).
Potential form of Group 3 verbs (生活する → 生活できる: can live).
This is because summers in Japan are hot, so houses where people could live comfortably and stay cool were necessary.
able to live, can lead a life
Conditional pattern expressing a natural consequence or inevitable result (when/if the entrance is large...).
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrasting meanings (cool in summer, but cold in winter).
Used to connect clauses indicating cause and effect.
When windows and entrances are large, a lot of breeze comes in during the summer, making it cool; however, in the winter it is cold, which makes it tough.
Passive form (たてる → たてられる: to be built).
The phrase '新しくたてられる' precedes and modifies the noun '家' (newly built houses).
However, newly built houses have changed considerably.
Connects adjectives together to list characteristics (both large and numerous).
Indicates a change of state over time (少なくなる: to become fewer).
Houses with large and numerous windows have become fewer.
to exist, to have, there is
Pattern expressing ability or potential (can live).
Expresses a change in state, from being unable to being able to do something (have become able to live comfortably...).
The て-form of a verb used to connect means or actions (by using electrical appliances...).
By using electrical appliances, people have become able to live cool in the summer and warm in the winter.
to live, to lead a life
can do, to be able to
default.tests.5.skills.0.sections.0.passages.1.s: Noun-modifying clause modifying the following noun (the postcard that was sent).
This is a picture postcard that Linh sent to her Japanese class teacher.
Expression used to convey anticipation or looking forward to an upcoming event.
day (read as よっか in 4日)
Honorific prefix expressing politeness and respect toward the other person.
Expresses an action currently in progress at the time of speaking (currently traveling).
Noun-modifying clause (a friend who is studying...).
Used with particle に to indicate a place of residence or living.
A friend of mine who is studying Japanese history at university lives in this town.
Comparative pattern: B more than A (likes this town more than Tokyo).
My friend likes this town more than Tokyo.
Passive form of the verb する (to be cherished, to be preserved).
Used at the end of a sentence to explain a reason or cause (it is because...).
I heard that... / reportedly (relaying hearsay information heard from a friend).
I heard it is because old things are cherished and taken care of.
Comparative pattern expressing preference: ...more / rather than (preferring Tokyo).
As for me, I prefer Tokyo.
Connecting form used to link two い-adjectives (both new and interesting).
That is because there are many new and interesting things.
new, fresh (connecting form with くて)
Particle に marking the recipient or target of an action (buying for/giving to the teacher).
I bought a small souvenir for you, Teacher.
default.tests.5.skills.0.sections.0.passages.2.s: Describes going somewhere to do something and then returning (in this case, going on the tour and returning).
Recently, I went on the 「Night Zoo Tour」.
went and returned, went and came back
Doing V2 after V1 (in this case, observing animals after sunset).
Used to explain or elaborate on what was mentioned in the previous sentence.
It is a tour to observe the animals after the sun sets.
Even if..., even though... Expresses concession (even if you visit the zoo during the daytime).
Lists representative actions or states (such as sleeping or not coming out).
Indicates that something happens occasionally or from time to time (sometimes regrettable things happen).
During the day, even if you go to the zoo, it can sometimes be disappointing because the animals are sleeping or do not come out into view.
there is, to happen, to occur
visible, can be seen, to be in sight
More than... / Compared to... (being active at night more than during the daytime).
Noun modification (plain form verb + noun): A verb in plain form precedes a noun to modify it (動く動物: animals that move/are active).
Among animals, there are some that are more active at night than during the day.
In order to, for the purpose of... (in order to see such animals).
Should do, had better do (advises going to the zoo after it gets dark).
Used to emphasize a conclusion or offer an explanatory recommendation.
To see such animals, it is better to go to the zoo after the sun sets.
to see, to look, to watch
to get dark, to set (of the sun)
default.tests.5.skills.0.sections.1.passages.0.s: A verb in negative plain form modifies the following noun (people who do not eat breakfast).
Expresses an ongoing change or continuous trend (is increasing).
The number of people who do not eat breakfast is increasing.
Suffix indicating an age group or decade (here, ages 20 to 29).
It is particularly increasing among young people in their 20s (ages 20–29).
Used for non-exhaustive listing of nouns ('such as... and...').
Hearsay form used to convey information heard from others ('I heard that...', 'it is said that...').
It is said that junior high school students who come to school early in the morning to exercise, or those who have no time to eat breakfast, are using this service.
early in the morning, early morning
junior high school student, middle school student
not exist, to not have, none
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrasting meaning ('... but...')
Causative form expressing making or letting someone perform an action ('to make/let eat')
Expresses the intention to make an effort to form a habit or change a state ('want to make an effort to...')
The children are delighted, but it is said that among parents there are also opinions such as, "I want to make sure they eat breakfast at home."
to feed, to make eat, to let eat
to exist, to have, there is
Indicates a ratio (3人に1人: 1 out of every 3 people).
Used to report hearsay or information heard from another source (I heard that...).
Indicates a habitual action or ongoing state (not eating breakfast).
It is said that among people in their 20s, one in three men and one in five women do not eat breakfast.
Used to ask a question or inquire about a reason in a gentle, polite manner.
Why is it that people don't eat breakfast?
Indicates a change in state for an i-adjective (became more / has increased).
Used at the end of a sentence to explain a reason or cause (because...).
Indicates an ongoing state or continuous action (staying up late).
That is because the number of people staying up late at night has increased.
Natural or inevitable conditional form: whenever the preceding action occurs, the resulting consequence inevitably follows (whenever..., if... then...).
Concessive conditional form (even if..., even though...).
Used to explain or clarify the background situation or reality of an event.
If you stay up late at night, you won't feel hungry even after waking up in the morning.
even if waking up, even when waking up
Indicates a deadline or time limit by which an action must be completed (by...).
Used to give advice or make a suggestion (it is good to do..., should...).
Used to convey hearsay or report information heard from others or expert advice.
It is said that at night, it is best to eat dinner by 8:00 and go to bed by 12:00.
Negative conditional form (if one does not...).
Expresses conjecture or assessment based on the situation (seems like, appears to).
It seems that there are also many people who cannot work or study well in the morning if they do not eat breakfast.
in the morning, during the morning
Indicates a change into a new state (to become, to get sick).
Used to emphasize a fact or provide explanatory background information.
Moreover, there are also many people who get sick.
Indicates an objective and polite reason or cause (because, since).
Expresses a decision made by an individual or group (decided to do).
At a certain junior high school, because the number of students who do not eat breakfast is increasing, they decided to provide meals at school once a week.
junior high school student, middle school student
default.tests.6.skills.0.sections.0.passages.0.s: Indicates the existence of an inanimate object or event at a location ('there is... at...')
There is an announcement about the summer festival in the classroom.
Noun-modifying clause qualifying a noun ('people who go...')
Those going to the summer festival, please gather at the station at 14:00.
Placed after a clause to indicate a cause or reason (because..., so...)
Used to list representative examples (such as..., and so on)
Used to make a polite request or instruction (please do...)
Because there is no place to park bicycles at the park, please use transportation such as trains.
there is not, to not exist, to not have
Indicates a change or transition to another date or state (changes to..., becomes...)
If it rains, the summer festival will be moved to July 22 (Sat).
if it rains, when it rains
to become, to turn into, to change to
default.tests.6.skills.0.sections.0.passages.1.s: Expresses the existence or location of an inanimate object or place (located in/at..., to be in/at...)
My house is in the countryside.
to be, to exist, to be located (for inanimate objects and places)
Used to list multiple reasons, qualities, or characteristics (not only..., but also...)
Indicates an approximate amount or extent (about 2 hours)
Used with negative forms to mean 'not very', 'hardly', or 'scarcely'
It takes about 2 hours by car to get to a town with department stores and movie theaters, and there are hardly any stylish shops or restaurants.
does not exist, there is not, not have
to exist, to have, to be
Indicates a specific time in the past or a life stage (when... / back when...)
Past negative form of a な-adjective (did not like...)
Therefore, when I was a child, I did not like the countryside.
Expresses a change of state (to become, to turn into)
Expresses a gradual change extending from the past up to the present (to gradually become...)
However, as I grew up, I gradually came to like this countryside.
To notice or realize a certain fact/matter
Placed at the end of a sentence to explain a reason or cause (because..., that is because...)
That is because I realized that the countryside has many good points.
realized, noticed (past form of 気がつく)
Comparative pattern of inferiority (A is not as... as B)
Conjunctive particle expressing contrast or concession (but, however)
Used to list multiple characteristics or reasons (not only..., but also...)
The countryside is not as convenient as the town, but it is quiet, and the water and vegetables are very delicious.
Sentence pattern expressing strong love or affection for the object marked by particle が
I love the countryside very much.
default.tests.6.skills.0.sections.0.passages.2.s: Sentence pattern indicating the existence of an inanimate object/event at a location (there is... at...)
There is a notice at the entrance of the library.
Honorific form of a Group 3 verb (利用する → 利用される) to show respect to library users
Particle indicating the recipient of information (to..., for...)
To those who use the library
Expresses finishing or completing an action (読み終わった: finished reading)
Polite request pattern asking someone to do something ("please...")
Please return the books you have finished reading to the reception desk.
Expresses chronological sequence: doing V2 after completing V1 (tidy up after using)
After using the desks and chairs, please be sure to tidy them up.
tidy up, clean up, put away
Verb combination expressing an accompanying action when returning (take along and go home)
Please take your trash home with you.
When / at the time of doing an action (when copying a book)
Doing the next action only after completing the first (inform the reception first, then copy)
When photocopying books, please inform the reception desk first before making copies.
Polite request or advice asking someone not to do something ("please do not...")
Please do not do the following inside the library.
Lists representative actions among others (actions like eating and drinking)
Nominalizes a verb (turning an action into a noun: eating and drinking)
Nominalizes a verb (turning an action into a noun: taking photos)
default.tests.6.skills.0.sections.0.passages.3.s: Relative clause modifying the following noun (the email that Mr. Tanaka sent).
This is an email that Mr. Tanaka sent to Mr. Kim.
Pattern used to convey hearsay or information heard from others ('I heard that...').
I heard that you are currently in South Korea, Mr. Kim.
Indicates a starting point and an ending point ('from... to...').
Expresses the speaker's intention or plan to do something ('thinking of doing...', 'planning to...').
I am planning to visit South Korea from the 23rd to the 27th.
Offers a soft suggestion or casual representative example ('or something', 'how about...').
Polite invitation or suggestion ('Won't you...?', 'Would you like to...?').
If it suits your schedule, Mr. Kim, would you like to have dinner together in the evening?
Someone does something as a favor for me (or my in-group).
Doing something in advance to prepare for the future ('to do beforehand').
If you let me know which day you can make it for a meal, I will book a restaurant in advance.
Nominalizes an action (the act of being able to meet).
Pattern expressing anticipation or looking forward to an upcoming event.
I am really looking forward to being able to meet Mr. Kim in South Korea.
can meet, to be able to meet (potential form of 会う)
default.tests.6.skills.0.sections.1.passages.0.s: Noun-modifying relative clause modifying the following noun (here '留学生が書いた' modifies '作文': an essay written by an international student).
This is an essay written by an international student.
Indicates a point of time in the past ('2 years ago').
I came to Japan two years ago.
Expresses an unintentional action or an outcome accompanied by regret ('ends up completely full of trash').
Indicates a change of state ('becomes full').
Therefore, the trash can at my house quickly ends up full of plastic waste.
Conditional pattern indicating that whenever an action occurs, a natural consequence follows ('whenever you do so...').
Used to list multiple characteristics or reasons ('both clean and convenient').
It is true that doing so keeps snacks and tomatoes clean and neat, and it is convenient for people living alone.
Lists representative actions (doing things like putting into bags, putting into containers, etc.).
Pattern expressing that there is no need to do something.
Used to express personal thoughts or opinions ('I think that...').
However, I do not think it is necessary to individually wrap snacks and tomatoes in plastic bags or put them in plastic containers.
Hypothetical conditional pattern 'if' (if not using..., then...).
If we don't use plastic or vinyl bags, (　　　).
if not using, if not used
Used to list multiple reasons, causes, or parallel characteristics ('not only convenient, but also...').
Expresses that something is easy to do ('生活しやすい': easy to live in, easy to manage daily life).
Expresses one's past thoughts or impressions ('thought that...').
I thought Japan was a very easy country to live in, and convenient because there are many convenience stores and supermarkets.
to have, to exist, there is
easy to do, easy to live
Expresses the existence of a certain fact or circumstance ('there is a thing/matter where...').
However, there is ① something regrettable.
Nominalizes a clause to explain or clarify the preceding subject ('It is a matter of...', 'That is...').
That is the fact that there is a lot of trash.
Indicates noticing or discovering a result while performing an action ('歩いていると': when walking around, you notice...).
Everywhere, in all places ('どこもきれい': clean everywhere).
When walking around town, there is almost no trash and everywhere is clean, but living in Japan produces a lot of garbage.
without, not having, there is not
Indicates discovering a result or state upon completing an action ('when I opened the box, I found that...').
Describes a resulting continuous state observed at that point in time ('was inside the bag').
For example, when I bought some sweets and opened the box, each piece was individually wrapped in a plastic bag.
Expresses an inevitable condition or natural consequence: whenever this action happens, that result follows ('eating one piece inevitably adds one piece of trash').
Expresses an unintended action carrying a sense of regret ('unfortunately ends up increasing trash').
Every time you eat one sweet, you end up creating another piece of trash.
Indicates that upon performing an action, one discovers or realizes something ('bought tomatoes and found that...').
Expresses an existing state resulting from an intentional action ('already placed', 'pre-wrapped').
The other day, when I bought tomatoes at the supermarket, they were placed in a plastic container and wrapped in plastic film.
Used to connect actions occurring in chronological sequence ('Go home and then cook...').
Both A and B ('both plastic containers and vinyl bags').
To become or turn into something ('turn into trash').
When I get home and cook, both the plastic containers and plastic bags all end up as trash.
default.tests.7.skills.0.sections.0.passages.0.s: Indicates discovering a situation or result after completing an action ('When... returned, [she] found...').
Describes a state resulting from an intentional action done in advance ('placed in advance').
Describes going somewhere and returning to the starting point ('coming home from school').
When Mika came home from school, this note was left on the desk.
Placed after the recipient's name at the start of a letter or note ('To...').
Indicates the purpose of movement (verb stem + に行く: 'go to do something').
Doing something and then returning ('go shopping and come back').
States a cause or reason gently and objectively ('because / since...')
Indicates a temporal condition or sequence ('after doing V1, then V2' / 'once...')
Expresses a polite request, instruction, or invitation ('please do... / please eat')
There are grapes in the refrigerator, so please eat them once you finish your homework.
Someone performs an action as a favor for the speaker or their family/in-group ('sent for me/us')
kindly sent (to me/us), sent as a favor
Suggests or invites the listener to do something together ('let's...')
To call someone on the phone (the recipient takes the particle に)
Placed after the sender's name at the end of a letter or note ('From...')
default.tests.7.skills.0.sections.0.passages.1.s: Purpose of movement: going somewhere to do something (verb stem + に行く / 行きました).
The other day, I went to eat ramen with a friend.
About to do something, attempting to do something (volitional form + とする).
Casual request or reminder not to do something: 'please don't...' (V-nai + で).
Describes an action that was ongoing at a specific point in the past.
Just as I was about to eat the ramen, my friend said, "Wait a second! Don't eat yet!" and took a lot of photos of the ramen.
was about to eat, tried to eat
a little, a bit, a moment
To finish doing something, to complete an action (verb stem + 終わる).
Expresses regret, sorrow, or an unintended action occurring.
Expresses a change of state: to become, to get (おいしくなくなる: to become no longer delicious).
By the time my friend finished taking photos, the hot ramen had cooled down and was no longer delicious.
unfortunately ended up becoming unappetizing, ended up no longer being delicious
Before doing something (dictionary form verb + 前に).
Expresses a trend or change that has been gradually progressing from the past up to the present (has come to, increasingly).
Recently, the number of people taking photos before eating their meal has been increasing.
before, in front of, prior to
Should do, ought to do (expresses what is natural, proper, or expected based on moral or common sense).
Expresses a request or wish for someone not to do something.
Expresses the speaker's personal thought, opinion, or view.
I think food should be eaten when it is at its most delicious, so I wish people would not do such things.
that kind of, such, like that
default.tests.7.skills.0.sections.0.passages.2.s: Expresses an ongoing action occurring at the present moment (doing something).
I am shopping on the internet.
Passive-form honorific verb, expressing respect toward the customer's actions.
Used after a noun to designate the recipient or audience of a notice or letter (to...).
to buy, to purchase (honorific form of 買う)
Conditional pattern 'if / when...', expressing an inevitable result that naturally follows a condition.
If you buy 3,000 yen or more, there is no shipping fee.
does not cost, free of charge
Expresses a sequence of actions: 'after doing V1, do V2'.
Potential form combined with humble language: 'can do... (for the customer/other party)'.
■ Products can be delivered 3 days after ordering.
Honorific form (sonkeigo) for Group 3 / Sino-Japanese verbal nouns, expressing respect toward the customer's action.
Expresses a condition or hypothetical situation: 'in case of...', 'in the event that...'.
■ If you use the next-day delivery service after placing an order, it costs 300 yen.
Expresses a hypothetical condition: 'in the event that one does V...', 'if/when doing V...'.
■ If you attach a message card, it costs 100 yen.
to attach, to include, to add
Negative potential pattern: 'cannot do N', 'unable to perform N'.
default.tests.7.skills.0.sections.0.passages.3.s: When, at the time of — used to specify the time an action takes place.
Expresses a habit or a recurring, repeated action.
I always sing songs when I drive a car.
Whenever / if... then... (expresses a condition leading to an inevitable or natural consequence).
To end up doing something (expresses regret or concern over an unintended result).
Might, may, perhaps (expresses roughly a 50% probability).
However, my mother says that if I sing while driving, I might cause an accident, so I should stop.
If it is... (noun + だったら: sets up a conditional assumption).
Even if... (expresses concession: even if this action is taken, still...).
And, besides / because... (used to list multiple reasons or characteristics).
If it's inside the car, singing isn't too loud, and it puts me in a really good mood.
In order to (do / not do something), so that — indicates purpose aimed at a desired state.
Have the experience of doing something (paired with 一度も...ない, it means 'never once').
I think that... (expresses a personal opinion or thought).
However, I am careful not to cause an accident, and since I have never caused an accident even once, I think I will be fine.
default.tests.7.skills.0.sections.1.passages.0.s: Expresses doing an action elsewhere and returning or bringing something back to the speaker's location.
「私が買ってきた」 modifies the noun 「おみやげ」 (the gift that I bought and brought back).
The souvenir I bought and brought was wine.
Expresses two actions occurring simultaneously (drinking wine while eating a meal).
Particle indicating the manner or number of people performing an action together (doing something all together as a group).
In my country, everyone eats meals together while drinking wine.
Negative potential form of the verb 飲む (unable to drink alcohol due to constitution or tolerance).
Used to list multiple reasons, states, or characteristics in parallel.
Sentence pattern expressing prohibition or lack of permission (not allowed to drink alcohol due to legal age).
However, Yamada's father and mother cannot drink alcohol, and Yamada and their younger sister are not allowed to drink alcohol yet.
must not drink, not allowed to drink
Used to directly or indirectly quote one's thoughts at that time (thought that...).
failed, made a mistake, messed up
Conditional pattern used to offer an opinion or recommendation based on a specified topic (if buying a souvenir...).
Expresses one's past thoughts or evaluation.
I thought that if buying a souvenir, ( ... ).
Indicates a reason or cause (because it was a rare wine...).
Expresses that someone did something beneficial for oneself, with a sense of gratitude.
However, Yamada's family said they were glad because it was a rare wine, and they happily received it with joy.
was pleased, was glad, was delighted
Grammar pattern used to list representative actions (doing things like making and eating takoyaki, playing games, and talking...).
Uses the て-form to connect actions in sequential order (making takoyaki and then eating).
And then, the whole family made and ate takoyaki, played games, and talked a lot together.
An い-adjective directly modifies a following noun (a fun day).
Polite past form of a noun predicate (it was a day...).
It was a very fun day.
Go somewhere to do something (e.g., go over to visit/hang out).
Last week, I went to visit Yamada's house.
Indicates an objective reason or cause (because it is far...).
Expresses obligation or necessity: must / have to do something (having to take the train and bus).
Yamada's house is far from my apartment, so I have to take the train and the bus.
Nominalizes the verb: turns an action into a noun phrase (taking/using the train and bus).
Conditional form ("if / when"): expresses a condition (if I take the wrong one...).
Expresses anxiety or indecision about what to do ("what should I do?").
Because it was my first time taking the train and bus, I was very worried: "What if I take the wrong train or bus? What should I do?".
first time, for the first time
if (I) make a mistake, if (I) take the wrong one
what should I do, what to do
Expresses a cause-and-effect relationship or an immediate subsequent action (as soon as...).
Indirect request; asking someone to do something (asking dad to come pick someone up).
Indicates that someone does something beneficial for the speaker or someone close to them.
When I told Yamada about ①that, Yamada kindly asked their father to drive to my apartment to pick me up.
come to pick up (for someone), come pick (someone) up
asked (for someone), requested as a favor
Expresses gratitude when someone does something beneficial for the speaker (kindly agreeing to the request).
Mr. Yamada's father immediately said, "②Of course, that's fine!"
Expresses that right upon arriving, a subsequent event occurs or is noticed.
Indicates that someone performs a welcoming action showing hospitality toward the speaker.
When I arrived at Yamada's house, Yamada's mother and high school younger sister welcomed me.
Indicates doing an action elsewhere and then returning with the result (buying a gift and bringing it back).
Volitional form used for invitations or suggestions to do something together (let's drink).
I handed Yamada's family the souvenir I bought in my home country and said, "Let's drink together!"
Expresses showing a certain facial expression or outward emotional look (a troubled expression).
Then, ③everyone had a slightly troubled look on their faces.
made a face, put on an expression, looked
default.tests.8.skills.0.sections.0.passages.0.s: To receive something from someone (in polite past form: もらいました).
A person participating in the town cleanup volunteer activity received this note.
To... (used in message or letter headers to indicate the recipient).
Sets the preliminary background or context before presenting the main point.
Indicates cause or reason (工事で: due to construction/repairs).
Negative potential form of the verb 使う (使えません: cannot use).
Regarding the town cleanup volunteer activity held every Saturday, the park where we usually gather is under construction, so it cannot be used.
Not A, but B (used to negate the former option to choose the latter).
To decide to do / choose something (expresses an intentional decision).
Therefore, starting next week, we decided to change the meeting place to the parking lot in front of the station instead of the park.
to gather, to assemble, to meet
Same as... / identical to... (pattern expressing similarity or equality).
The time remains the same as usual.
Polite request or instruction pattern ('please do...').
Connects two actions in chronological order (bring a trash bag and then come).
Please bring a trash bag and come to the parking lot at 9:00 AM.
Nominalizes a clause: 'the thing/matter that...' (わからないこと: things that are unclear / what you do not understand).
Polite request or instruction pattern (please contact).
If there is anything you do not understand, please contact Mr./Ms. Tanaka.
do not understand, not know, unclear
if there is, if you have
default.tests.8.skills.0.sections.0.passages.1.s: Say that..., believe that... (quotes an opinion or thought)
There are people who say that they do not drink alcohol because it is bad for their health.
When..., whenever... (expresses a condition leading to an inevitable or natural result)
Can do, to be able to do (indicates ability or possibility to perform an action)
Say that..., state that... (quotes another person's opinion)
However, there are also people who say that drinking alcohol improves your mood and can reduce stress.
can do, to be able to
To continue doing something, to keep doing (verb stem + 続ける)
Let's... (advice, invitation, or polite call to action)
However, let's avoid drinking alcohol every day continuously or drinking a large amount in one sitting.
Without doing V1, instead of doing V1 / doing something without...
Way of doing, how to do (verb stem + 方)
Also, drinking alcohol without eating anything is bad for your body, so please be careful.
way of drinking, manner of drinking
default.tests.8.skills.0.sections.0.passages.2.s: Expresses a state resulting from an intentional action done in advance (〜が置いてある: has been placed/left).
This note was left on Mr. Yamakawa's desk.
Divider line indicating the start of the message note.
Used after the recipient's name at the beginning of a letter or note (To... / Dear...).
Attached to an adjective stem to indicate an excessive degree (せますぎる: too cramped).
Indicates an objective and polite reason or cause (because..., so...).
Polite request pattern asking someone to do something (could you please... for me?).
The room for today's meeting is too small, so could you please change it to a slightly larger room?
Noun-modifying relative clause using a verb in dictionary form (会議で使うパソコン: computer used in the meeting).
Doing something in advance in preparation for the future (用意しておきます: will prepare in advance).
I will prepare the computer to be used for the meeting in advance.
Nominalizing an action using verb dictionary form + の (コピーするの: photocopying).
Expresses gratitude for someone doing a favor (手伝ってくれました: helped me).
Tanaka helped me photocopy the documents.
Doing something in advance for preparation or maintaining a state (置いておきます: will leave in advance).
I will leave the documents on the desk.
will put in advance, will leave
Expresses conjecture or anticipation about an impending situation (長くなりそう: looks like it will run long).
Conjunction indicating a transition or mild contrast (but, although).
Volitional form suggesting or inviting action together (let's...).
Today's meeting looks like it will be long, but let's do our best.
looks like it will become, seems likely to become
let's do our best, let's work hard
Divider line indicating the end of the message.
default.tests.8.skills.0.sections.0.passages.3.s: Indicates the starting point in time of an action (from last month).
I started a part-time job at the zoo last month.
Lists representative actions among others (doing things like guiding visitors and explaining about the animals).
Indicates a topic or subject matter (about animals).
Used to define or explain the content of something (the job is to...).
My job is to guide visitors who come to the zoo and explain the animals to them.
Expresses an aim or purpose (so that the children can understand).
Expresses two simultaneous actions performed by the same subject (talking while showing pictures).
Expresses a conscious effort or habitual action (making an effort to speak clearly).
For the children, I make an effort to speak clearly while showing pictures and photos so that they can understand many things about animals.
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrasting meanings; 'but', 'although' (e.g., busy, but very enjoyable).
て-form expressing a cause or reason leading to an emotion (e.g., feeling happy because of being able to meet).
I am busy every day, but it is very fun because I get to see cute animals.
able to meet, can meet (potential form of 会う)
default.tests.8.skills.0.sections.1.passages.0.s: Expresses an action continuing throughout the entire duration of another ongoing action ('while listening...').
While listening to someone speak, Japanese people give a lot of conversational responses (aizuchi).
give conversational responses, make listener feedback, nod along
Used to define or explain the meaning of a concept ('A means B').
Lists representative actions among others ('doing things like saying..., nodding...').
Giving conversational responses (aizuchi) means repeatedly saying things like "uh-huh", "oh really?", or "that's right", or nodding one's head up and down.
give conversational responses, make listener feedback, nod along
saying (among other things), such as saying
up and down, above and below
Used to quote or state specific contents ('that...', 'saying that...').
Indicates purpose or intended use ('something used for...').
Aizuchi is something used to convey messages like "I am listening to you" and "Please, go ahead and keep talking."
purpose, for the sake of, in order to
Verb stem (masu form without masu) + 終わる: Finish doing, complete an action (finish speaking).
Advises someone not to do something (had better not say anything).
Indicates a time limit or endpoint ("until...").
However, in other countries, there are also cultures where people think it is better to look the other person in the eye and say nothing until they finish speaking.
Expresses that an occasion or situation sometimes occurs ("if there happens to be an occasion to talk").
Verb stem (masu form without masu) + 続ける: Continue or maintain an action continuously (keep saying).

If that person and a Japanese person were to converse, to the foreigner speaking, because the Japanese person listening keeps saying words like "yeah, yeah" and "yes, yes," there are probably some who would find it ① noisy and annoying.
if there is, if it happens
Expresses an unintentional state or spontaneous feeling (e.g., inadvertently feeling anxious).
Expresses a personal thought or opinion gently and politely ("I think that perhaps...", "I wonder if...").
Conversely, when Japanese people are speaking, because foreigners do not nod or give conversational responses, I think they often end up feeling ② anxious.
on the contrary, conversely, in contrast
to think, to feel, to consider
end up thinking, end up feeling
Connects two clauses to indicate an inevitable or natural result ("whenever...", "when...").
When cultures differ, communication methods also differ.
Used to give advice on what one should do (e.g., should think about / consider the method).
Nominalizes the preceding clause ("the fact that the way of conveying is different").
Therefore, between Japanese people and foreigners, one should understand that the way of conveying 「（　　　）」 is different, and consider how to communicate.
to convey, to communicate, to report
Dual concession pattern ("whether... or not...", "even if... or even if not...").
Expresses a grounded expectation or strong conviction ("should certainly be...", "ought to be...").
Potential form of the verb する (to be able to communicate).
If you do so, whether you give conversational responses (nod along) or not, you should certainly be able to communicate pleasantly.
if so, doing so, that way
even if responding, even if giving a response
even if not responding, even if not giving a response
can do, to be able to
should be, expected to, ought to
default.tests.9.skills.0.sections.0.passages.0.s: Expresses doing something in advance for preparation or maintaining a state.
This note and the book are left on Ali's desk.
to place in advance, to leave (something) in place
Indicates the source or person from whom something is received or borrowed (borrowed from Ali).
Expresses doing an action in advance as preparation (placing books here in advance).
I am leaving the book I borrowed from Ali.
to leave (in advance), to put down in advance
thank you very much (for a past action)
Expresses a desire to do something (wanting to borrow).
Quotes what someone said or expressed previously (said that...).
I am also leaving here together the book that Ali said he wanted to borrow.
to want to borrow, wanting to borrow
to put, to place, to leave
Indicates an objective reason or cause with a gentle, polite nuance (because...).
Expresses 'only', always used with a negative verb form to emphasize small quantity (only brought 2 books).
Expresses doing an action and moving toward the speaker (to bring).
Because they were heavy, I only brought 2 books today.
Expresses carrying or bringing something toward the speaker/here (to bring).
Next week, I will bring the other 3 books.
default.tests.9.skills.0.sections.0.passages.1.s: When / at the time of doing something (indicates the timing of an action or event)
Precautions when playing in the park
Indicates an ongoing or continuous state of something (the park is open)
From ~ (indicates the starting point in time)
The park is open from 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM.
Except for / other than ~ (indicates an excluded item or time)
Negative potential form of a verb (入れません: cannot enter)
You cannot enter outside of these hours.
Non-exhaustive listing of nouns (such as bicycles, motorcycles, etc.)
◆ Please park bicycles and motorcycles at the park entrance.
put in, bring in, take inside
◆ You must not do the following inside the park.
Using / with ~ as a tool or means to do something
Verb nominalization (turns the action 'play' into 'the act of playing')
・Playing with a ball (using a ball to play)
Verb nominalization (turns the action 'smoke' into 'the act of smoking')
default.tests.9.skills.0.sections.0.passages.2.s: Noun-modifying clause (届いたメール: received email)
This is an email sent from Professor Yamada to Tom.
Used to introduce background context before getting to the main point ('Regarding the appointment... but').
Must do, have to do (expresses obligation or necessity).
Change of state (なければならなくなる: to end up in a situation where one must attend).
Regarding our appointment tomorrow (the 30th), it turns out I have to attend a meeting.
ended up having to attend, have to attend
Used to make a polite request or invitation ('Could you...?', 'Would you be able to...?').
So, I am very sorry, but could we reschedule our appointment to 3:00 PM on the 31st?
excuse me, but; I am sorry, but
can we change?, could it be rescheduled?
Conditional form: If... (都合がよければ: If it is convenient / If your schedule permits).
Indicates an ongoing state or readiness for an upcoming action (waiting / will be waiting).
If it is convenient for you, Tom, I will be waiting in my office.
Conditional / temporal sequence pattern: After / once doing... (読んだら: after reading).
Used to make a polite request ('please give / please provide a reply').
Once you read this email, please reply.
default.tests.9.skills.0.sections.0.passages.3.s: Expresses an occupation or ongoing state of employment (working at...).
Particle indicating the location where an action takes place (working at the library).
Ms. Ishida works at Kawashita Library.
Used to list representative actions among others ('doing things like... and...').
Embeds an indirect question within a larger sentence (e.g., considering where it is best to place which book).
She handles book consultations and considers where best to place each book.
Lists representative actions (doing things like writing introductions, reading picture books, etc.).
Particle indicating the recipient or target of an action (reading to the children).
In addition, she writes recommendations for good books in the library newsletter and reads picture books to young children.
default.tests.9.skills.0.sections.1.passages.0.s: Indicates the number of people or group performing an action together (together with family).
Noun modification: the preceding clause modifies the noun (the hotel located in the mountains).
This summer, I stayed with my family at Hotel ① in the mountains.
in the mountains, deep in the mountains
to be, to be located, to exist
Indicates the starting point and ending point of a route (from the station to the bus stop).
Follows a quantity or counter to express '... or more', 'more than...'.
From the station to the bus stop near the hotel, it took more than 2 hours by bus.
more than 2 hours, 2 hours or more
At night, the stars were very beautiful.
Indicates that throughout the entire period the state in the preceding clause continues (staying at the hotel), the actions in the following clause occur continuously or repeatedly.
Sentence pattern used to list representative actions (going for walks, swimming, catching insects, taking naps).
While staying at the hotel, every day we all went for walks, swam in the lake, caught insects, and took naps together.
We stayed at the hotel for 1 week.
Attaches to the verb stem (Masu-form without Masu) to express two actions occurring simultaneously (e.g., returning home while chatting).
Uses the particle と to quote direct speech enclosed in brackets 「」.
We returned home while saying, "That was fun, wasn't it? ② Living like this once in a while is nice, too."
this kind of, such, like this
occasionally, once in a while, sometimes
The particle を is used with motion verbs to indicate the path or space passed through.
Indicates an approximation close to a certain amount of time or quantity (nearly 30 minutes).
From the bus stop to the hotel, we walked along a narrow road for nearly 30 minutes.
Connects an い-adjective to another adjective to list characteristics (both small and old).
Conjunction connecting two clauses with a contrasting or concessive meaning (although... but...).
The hotel was small and old, but the inside was very clean.
Used with a negative predicate to completely negate both items or options (neither of them is available).
do not have, there is no
Emphatically lists items sharing the same negative state (neither... nor...).
In addition, there is neither a refrigerator nor an air conditioner.
do not have, there is no
Polite past negative form of な-adjectives and nouns (was not...).
Potential form of the verb する, indicating the ability to perform an action (could do, was able to do).
This hotel was not convenient, but we were able to do many things at the mountains and the lake.
could do, was able to do
Expresses that the action in the subsequent clause occurs immediately after or as a natural consequence of the preceding action (opening the window caused the breeze to blow in).
Indicates movement directed toward the speaker or the space where the speaker is located (blew into the room).
When I put my luggage in the room and opened the window, a cool breeze came in from the lake.
Indicates chronological order: performing a subsequent action after completing a prior one (after resting for a bit).
Indicates an objective, natural cause or reason (because it was still light out).
Indicates the purpose of going out (going out for the purpose of taking a walk).
After resting for a bit, since it was still light outside, I went out for a walk.
The て-form of an い-adjective, used to connect and list characteristics or states.
The particle も adds supplementary information in the same vein (the scenery was also beautiful).
The air was fresh, and the scenery was also beautiful.
